speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring and on what scale from 1 to 10 would you rate your pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture)

The history of forceful vomiting (retching), followed by choking, coughing, and subsequent chest pain in a patient who consumed a significant amount of alcohol is highly suggestive of an esophageal rupture. Given the potential for mediastinitis and sepsis, this is a surgical emergency. I need to confirm your suspicion with imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray (upright and left lateral decubitus).
